title: Phosphate backbone epitranscriptomics: Discovery of natural RNA phosphorothioates and their writer machinery.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC record (PMID 42753734): not open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no text-mined data accessions (only RRIDs for software tools), no NCBI GEO/SRA/BioProject links, no Zenodo/Dryad hit on the DOI. Two GEO searches ('RNA phosphorothioate archaea', 'phosphorothioate tRNA') returned 0 datasets.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the content: sequencing and mass-spectrometry maps of RNA phosphorothioate (PS, sulfur swapped for a backbone oxygen) sites in archaeal rRNA and tRNA hotspots, a writer enzyme family, and its presence/absence across species. Only the abstract was readable; no site counts are given.

a1_downloadable.note: No data deposit found: no accession in Europe PMC annotations, no NCBI links, no GEO hit, no Zenodo/Dryad record; paper is paywalled with no PMC copy. Checked repositories, not files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Unverifiable; a per-nucleotide 'PS site yes/no' label would have to be built from raw sequencing reads that we could not locate.

a3_inputs_present.note: No files found; rRNA/tRNA sequences would be retrievable from genomes, but the site calls are not.

a5_enough_rows.note: Abstract describes PS 'hotspots' in rRNA and tRNA across a few archaeal species, which suggests tens of sites, far under 400 labelled examples. Count not seen.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Processed site tables would be tiny if they existed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts available from either paper or files.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would be physical measurements (sequencing plus mass spectrometry), not model output, per the abstract.

backbone.name: RNA-FM (RNA language model) would be the natural fit

integration.partner_dataset: MODOMICS (RNA modification database) or GTDB (archaeal genome taxonomy) for writer-enzyme presence/absence
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Can the presence of the writer enzyme across archaeal genomes predict which species carry backbone sulfur modifications?

honest_claim_h3: Not reachable: with no deposited site table and likely only tens of sites, no model claim could be made.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use RNA sequence around each backbone position to predict where natural sulfur-for-oxygen modifications occur in archaeal transfer and ribosomal RNA.
plain_idea.train_on: Windows of tRNA/rRNA sequence centred on each position, from a few archaeal species; number of modified sites unknown (no data found).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the position carries a phosphorothioate, as measured by the paper's sequencing and mass-spectrometry mapping.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would let researchers scan other archaeal genomes for likely modification sites before running costly mapping, but the site count is probably too small to learn from.

label_elsewhere.sources: None known; the paper claims this is the first natural RNA backbone modification detected, so no public resource (e.g. MODOMICS) holds these labels yet.
label_elsewhere.why: No external labelled data exists to expand training or validate a model.

ml_idea: Sequence-context classifier for RNA phosphorothioate sites, or genome-level presence/absence of the writer enzyme; neither is feasible without deposited data and with a likely tiny site count.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find the data availability statement on the Cell page and count the mapped PS sites; under a few hundred kills it.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: paywalled discovery paper with no deposited data found (no accessions, no GEO, no Zenodo/Dryad). A5 also likely fails, since the abstract describes a handful of rRNA/tRNA hotspots rather than thousands of labelled sites.
